name: Highbanks Metro Park
what: Hike to an observation deck 100 feet above the Olentangy River, or take the kids to the nature center's bird-feeder windows and the 15-acre natural play area. Big Meadows is a top sledding hill in winter.
when: 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar; nature center 9am-8pm (Apr-Sep) / 9am-6pm (Oct-Mar)

name: Blendon Woods Metro Park
what: Short easy trails lead to Thoreau Lake's two heated observation shelters with spotting scopes for watching ducks and geese. Also has an inclusive playground, a natural play area, free disc golf and an ice-skating pond.
address: 4265 E Dublin Granville Rd, Columbus, OH 43081
when: 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar; nature center 9am-8pm (Apr-Sep) / 9am-6pm (Oct-Mar)

name: Sharon Woods Metro Park
what: A 3.8-mile paved loop that is great for first bike rides, plus a 7.5-acre wooded natural play area where kids can climb and creek-stomp. Schrock Lake fishing, two sledding hills and several playgrounds.
when: 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar

name: Inniswood Metro Gardens
what: Manicured rose, herb and woodland gardens on short paved and boardwalk trails, with the 2.8-acre Sisters' Garden built specifically for kids to explore. One of the prettiest free spots in the area.
when: 6:30am-9pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-7pm Oct-Mar

name: Slate Run Metro Park
what: Big grassland and wetland park minutes from Canal Winchester with sandhill cranes, a stocked 14-acre lake, observation decks on the Kokomo wetland trail and a natural play area. Pair it with the historical farm next door.
address: 1375 State Route 674 N, Canal Winchester, OH 43110
when: 6:30am to dark, year-round

name: Slate Run Living Historical Farm
what: Working 1880s farm where costumed staff do real chores and kids can see Percheron horses, pigs, geese and turkeys up close, then tour the 1856 farmhouse. One of the best free kid outings in central Ohio.
address: 1375 State Route 674 N, Canal Winchester, OH 43110
when: Tue-Thu & Sun 9am-6pm, Fri-Sat 9am-7pm (Apr-Sep); Tue-Thu & Sun 9am-5pm, Fri-Sat 9am-sunset (Oct-Mar); closed Mon; Jan-Mar grounds/barn only

name: Chestnut Ridge Metro Park
what: Climb the Ridge Trail about 150 feet to the first Appalachian foothill for a view back toward Columbus, or fish the 2-acre pond. Quiet, close to Canal Winchester, with two free picnic shelters.
when: 6:30am to dark, year-round

name: Walnut Woods Metro Park
what: Flat paved loops (Buckeye 2 mi, Monarch 1.4 mi, Sweetgum 2.6 mi) ideal for strollers, scooters and kid bikes, plus a dog park and the shady Tall Pines picnic area.
when: 6:30am to dark, year-round

name: Pickerington Ponds Metro Park
what: Wetland preserve with five observation decks where 260+ bird species have been logged; good odds of herons, ducks, deer and beaver. Short walks, so it works with little legs.
when: 6:30am to dark, year-round

name: Three Creeks Metro Park
what: Where Alum, Big Walnut and Blacklick creeks meet; paved greenway access, Heron and Turtle Pond loops, a playground at the shelter house and a 12-acre pine-forest natural play area.
when: 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar

name: Scioto Audubon Metro Park & Free Climbing Wall
what: Downtown riverfront park with a 35-foot outdoor climbing wall that is free to use (bring your own harness; four auto-belays spring to fall), plus an obstacle course, playgrounds, sand volleyball, dog park and the Grange Audubon Center.
when: Park 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar; wall 8am-9pm Apr-Sep, 8am-7pm Oct-Mar; under 16 needs an adult

name: Battelle Darby Creek Metro Park (Bison)
what: See a real bison herd roaming two prairie pastures from the flat gravel Darby Creek Greenway or the nature center, which also has a 53-foot indoor living stream. Also the east trailhead for the Camp Chase rail trail.
when: 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar; nature center 9am-8pm (Apr-Sep) / 9am-6pm (Oct-Mar)

name: Blacklick Woods Metro Park & Canopy Walk
what: Walk a boardwalk 40 feet up in the treetops with rope bridges and a treehouse (elevator available), then hit the nature center's wildlife windows. Easy swamp-forest trails and sledding in winter.
when: 6:30am-10pm Apr-Sep, 6:30am-8pm Oct-Mar; nature center 9am-8pm (Apr-Sep) / 9am-6pm (Oct-Mar)

name: Clear Creek Metro Park
what: Ohio's largest nature preserve: sandstone cliffs, hemlock ravines and rhododendron on eleven trails from 0.3 to 2.5 miles, with fishing at Lake Ramona. A Hocking Hills feel without the crowds or the drive.
when: 6:30am to dark, year-round

name: Quarry Trails Metro Park
what: Former quarry turned park with the 25-foot Millikin Falls (0.6-mile trail with steep steps), quarry lakes you can fish or paddle, and free sport-climbing routes with waiver and helmet. The via ferrata is a paid program.
cost: Free (via ferrata is a paid program)
when: 6:30am to dark, year-round

name: Scioto Mile Fountain & Bicentennial Park
what: Downtown's big interactive fountain where kids run through jets with the skyline behind them; swim diapers required for the untrained. The Dorrian Green fountain across the river (50 S Belle St) is another free option.
address: 233 S Civic Center Dr, Columbus, OH 43215
when: Seasonal: fountain daily 11am-7pm late May to early Sep; sensory-friendly hour Mon 11am-noon; park open year-round

name: Goodale Park
what: Victorian Village's classic park with a pond, gazebo, playground and courts, a short walk from the Short North. Good stroller loop before or after a Gallery Hop.
when: 7am-11pm daily

name: Schiller Park & Actors' Theatre
what: German Village's park has a playground, stocked pond and amphitheater where Actors' Theatre of Columbus stages free professional outdoor plays every summer. Bring a blanket and a picnic.
when: Park 7am-11pm daily; plays are seasonal (summer) - see theactorstheatre.org for dates

name: Topiary Park
what: The only topiary re-creation of a painting anywhere: Seurat's 'A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte' in shrubs, with a pond standing in for the Seine. Quick, free, and odd enough to delight kids.
when: Dawn to dusk daily (site also lists 7am-11pm)

name: Columbus Park of Roses (Whetstone Park)
what: One of the largest public rose gardens in the country, inside Whetstone Park with playgrounds and direct Olentangy Trail access. Peak roses are typically June; the park is lovely year-round.
when: 7am to dusk, year-round

name: Franklin Park
what: The 88-acre city park wrapped around the Conservatory: a 1.1-mile paved loop, fishing pond, playground and amphitheater. Free any day, and a natural pairing with a Community Day visit next door.
when: 7am-11pm daily; the Cascades water feature was closed for repair as of mid-2026

name: Columbus Commons
what: Downtown lawn with free Family Movie Nights and the Local & Live concert series in summer, a carousel the site lists as a free ride, and the Thursday Downtown farmers market. Wanderlights holiday lights are free in Nov-Dec.
cost: Free (nearly all events free; garage parking extra)
when: Park 7am-11pm daily; movies/concerts seasonal (summer) - check columbuscommons.org

name: Franklin Park Conservatory - Community Day
what: Normally $25 for adults, but Franklin County and City of Columbus residents get in free the first Sunday of every month with photo ID and proof of address. Includes the gardens, glasshouses, Hot Shop glassblowing and daytime exhibits.
cost: Free first Sunday for Franklin County residents (otherwise about $25 adult / $17 child 3-12)
when: Community Day: first Sunday monthly, 10am-5pm (10am-4pm Nov-Jan); no advance reservations; evening events excluded

name: Columbus Museum of Art
what: Free all day every Sunday, and visitors 25 and under (plus one accompanying adult for kids) are always free. Big, bright galleries, a kid-friendly Wonder Room and the Walter sculpture garden.
cost: Free Sundays; 25 and under always free; otherwise $22 adult ($5 Thu 5-9pm Oct-May)
when: Tue-Wed & Fri-Sun 10am-5pm, Thu 10am-9pm, closed Mon; free Sundays

name: Wexner Center for the Arts
what: OSU's contemporary art center with rotating exhibitions in a landmark Eisenman building; gallery admission is free for everyone. Good rainy-day stop with older kids.
when: Tue-Wed 9:30am-5pm, Thu-Fri 9:30am-7pm, Sat 10am-5pm, Sun 10am-4pm; closed Mon, between exhibitions and on OSU home football days

name: Ohio Statehouse Free Tours
what: Free guided tours of the 1861 capitol leave from the Map Room hourly on weekdays; see the rotunda, House and Senate chambers and the museum education center. Groups under 10 just show up.
when: Weekday walk-in tours on the hour 10am-3pm; weekends noon, 1, 2 and 3pm; none on state holidays

name: Billy Ireland Cartoon Library & Museum
what: The world's largest collection of comics and cartoon art, with rotating gallery shows at OSU's Sullivant Hall. Free, small and fun for comic-loving kids.
when: Galleries generally afternoons (1-5pm listed); check site for current days

name: Decorative Arts Center of Ohio
what: Rotating design and decorative-arts exhibitions in the 1835 Reese-Peters House on Lancaster's Main Street. Free admission, with a kid-friendly hands-on studio room in most shows.
when: Wed-Fri 11am-4pm, Sat-Sun 1-4pm; closed Mon-Tue

name: Sherman House Museum
what: Birthplace of Civil War general William T. Sherman and Senator John Sherman, with guided tours of the restored 1811 house. Cheap, quick and a good local-history stop in downtown Lancaster.
when: Seasonal: Apr 15-Dec 6, Wed-Sat tours at noon, 1, 2 and 3pm

name: The Georgian Museum
what: Guided tours of an 1832 Georgian mansion furnished to period, a block from the Sherman House. A combo 'Beauty & Brawn' ticket covers both for $10.
cost: $6 adult / $2 under 18 ($10 combo with Sherman House)
when: Seasonal: Apr 15-Dec 6, Wed-Sat tours at noon, 1, 2 and 3pm

name: Ohio Glass Museum & Glass Blowing Studio
what: Lancaster's glassmaking history (Anchor Hocking country) plus live glassblowing demos in the hot shop during open hours. Kids love watching molten glass get shaped.
when: Wed-Sun noon-4pm; demos during open hours (call 740-687-0101 to confirm)

name: The Wagnalls Memorial
what: A Tudor-Gothic castle of a library in tiny Lithopolis, gifted by the Funk & Wagnalls family, with children's programs, gardens and a community theater. Free to visit and browse like any library.
when: Mon & Thu 10am-8pm, Tue 10am-5pm, Wed & Sat 10am-2pm; closed Fri & Sun

name: Motts Military Museum
what: Groveport museum packed with vehicles, aircraft, a WWII Higgins boat and galleries from the Revolution through Desert Storm and NASA. Kids 5 and under are free.
when: Tue-Sat 9am-5pm, Sun 1-5pm; closed Mon

name: Ohio History Center & Ohio Village
what: State history museum with a mastodon, Ohio's natural history and a recreated 19th-century village (Ohio Village, included with admission when open). Not cheap, but kids 3 and under are free.
when: Wed-Sun 10am-5pm; confirm Ohio Village status before going

name: COSI
what: Columbus's big science center on the riverfront. Listed for price reference: it is not cheap, though under-2s are free and a Museums for All rate exists for SNAP/EBT households.
cost: $30 adult / $25 ages 2-12 online (+$5 at door); under 2 free
when: Check cosi.org/hours-calendar; 5% arts fee added to tickets

name: North Market Downtown
what: Historic public market with 30-some independent food vendors, bakers and a produce stand; free to wander and cheap to graze. Stroller-friendly throughout.
cost: Free to enter (paid garage at 45 Vine St)
when: Tue-Sat 9am-7pm, Sun-Mon 10am-5pm

name: Clintonville Farmers Market
what: One of the city's biggest Saturday producer-only markets, on N High Street in Clintonville, a short hop from the Park of Roses. Live music and kid activities most weeks.
when: Seasonal: Saturdays 9am-noon, late April to late November

name: Worthington Farmers Market
what: Large Saturday market along High Street in Old Worthington's historic district, with the village green and shops right there. A reliable summer-morning outing.
when: Seasonal: Saturdays 8am-noon, May through October

name: Canal Winchester Farmers Market
what: Small-town Saturday market in Stradley Park on downtown's High Street, steps from the Barber Museum and the Interurban Depot historical marker.
address: 30 S High St, Canal Winchester, OH 43110
when: Seasonal: Saturdays 9am-noon, late May to late September

name: Columbus Metropolitan Library - Main Library
what: Grand downtown library with an 800-seat reading room, a big children's area and free weekly story times across the system (Canal Winchester branch is at 123 Groveport Rd). Great free indoor hours on a bad-weather day.
when: Mon-Thu 9am-9pm, Fri-Sat 9am-6pm, Sun 1-5pm; story time schedule by branch at columbuslibrary.org

name: Fairfield County District Library - Main (Lancaster)
what: Lancaster's main library runs free Family Storytime (ages 6 and under, no registration) with weekly themes, songs and crafts, plus a dedicated second-floor storytime area. Branches in Baltimore, Bremen, Amanda and more.
when: Mon-Thu 9am-8pm, Fri-Sat 9am-5pm, Sun 1-5pm; program schedule in the Events list above

name: Pickerington Public Library
what: Free early-literacy classes like Rhyme Time (0-23 months) and other storytimes at the Main Library, plus the Sycamore Plaza branch on Refugee Road near Canal Winchester.
when: Mon-Thu 9am-8pm, Fri 9am-6pm, Sat 9am-5pm, Sun noon-5pm; program schedule in the Events list above

name: Short North Gallery Hop
what: First Saturday of every month the galleries along High Street stay open late with street performers, chalk artists and public art. Free to wander; early evening is the kid-friendly window.
address: High St (Short North Arts District), Columbus, OH 43201
when: First Saturday monthly, 4-8pm, year-round

name: National Barber Museum & Hall of Fame
what: Quirky Canal Winchester museum of antique barber chairs, poles, razors and shaving mugs; a quick and cheap downtown stop. The Interurban Depot historical marker is two blocks away on S High St.
when: Fri-Sat 11am-4pm; Mon-Thu by appointment

name: Ohio Railway Museum
what: Saturday-only summer museum in Worthington where admission includes unlimited rides in a vintage coach pulled by an Army locomotive. Pricey-ish but a guaranteed hit with train-loving toddlers.
when: Seasonal: Saturdays 11am-5pm, May through late September

name: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium
what: Not cheap, but Franklin County residents pay about $10 less per ticket with ID, under-3s are free, and the zoo runs Franklin County Community Days with discounted admission (dates on its calendar). CML's Culture Pass can get a family in free.
cost: About $25 adult / $19 child 3-9 (Franklin Co. resident rate); +$12 parking
when: Daily; hours vary by season; check Community Day dates and Culture Pass availability

name: Olentangy Trail
what: About 14 miles of paved riverside trail from Worthington through OSU to downtown, with easy family segments at Whetstone Park, Antrim Park and Tuttle Park. Links to the Scioto Trail for a longer ride.
address: Whetstone Park trailhead, 3923 N High St, Columbus, OH 43214
when: Dawn to dusk, year-round

name: Alum Creek Trail
what: 24.5-mile paved greenway from Westerville down through Columbus to Three Creeks Park, the closest long trail to the southeast side. Trailheads with parking at Three Creeks, Wolfe Park, Innis Park and Academy Park.
address: Three Creeks trailhead, 3860 Bixby Rd, Groveport, OH 43125
when: Dawn to dusk, year-round

name: Canal Winchester Trail System
what: Nearly 5 miles of asphalt path linking Canal Winchester neighborhoods, downtown and the pool, with a spur to the Bergstresser/Dietz Covered Bridge, Franklin County's last covered bridge. Park at Hanners Park or Westchester Park.
address: Hanners Park, 458 Groveport Rd, Canal Winchester, OH 43110
when: Dawn to dusk, year-round

name: Hayden Falls Park
what: A 35-foot waterfall in a gorge inside the city limits, reached by a short boardwalk and stairs to an overlook. Tiny lot, big payoff, especially after rain or a deep freeze.
when: Daylight hours, year-round; small lot fills on weekends

name: Rising Park & Mt. Pleasant
what: Lancaster's signature hike: a short, steep scramble up a Blackhand sandstone bluff to a 250-foot overlook of the whole town. Playground, catch-and-release pond and picnic areas at the bottom.
when: Daily 8am-8pm

name: Alley Park (Charles Alley Nature Park)
what: Roughly 300-acre Lancaster city park with two lakes, six miles of wooded trails and the Goslin Nature Education Center, which runs family programs like maple tapping and pumpkin hikes.
address: 2805 Old Logan Rd SE, Lancaster, OH 43130
when: Daylight hours; nature center hours vary (740-681-5025)

name: Shallenberger State Nature Preserve
what: Short loop trail to the top of Allen Knob, a sandstone outcrop with mountain laurel and a nice vista. Small, quiet and about a mile of hiking, right on Lancaster's west side.
address: 2468 Becks Knob Rd SW, Lancaster, OH 43130
when: Open daily, dawn to dusk

name: Wahkeena Nature Preserve
what: Fairfield County Parks preserve with a nature center, a floating boardwalk over Lake Odonata full of dragonflies and turtles, resident education raptors (a screech owl and red-shouldered hawk) and three easy-to-moderate trails.
address: 2200 Pump Station Rd SE, Sugar Grove, OH 43155
when: Seasonal: Wed-Sun 8am-4:30pm, mid-March to mid-November; closed winter

name: Stebelton Park at Rock Mill
what: Restored 1824 gristmill with a 26-foot wooden waterwheel, a 1901 covered bridge over a gorge waterfall and free mill tours on summer weekends, with live milling the last Sunday of the month.
when: Park dawn-dusk year-round; mill open May-Oct Wed & Sat 11am-2pm, Sun 1-4pm

name: Mambourg Park
what: 116 acres east of Lancaster with four trails including a quarter-mile barrier-free loop and a 1940s stone nature center whose observation room looks out on a pond and bird feeders.
when: Park dawn-dusk year-round; nature center Fri-Sat 10am-2pm

name: Smeck Park
what: Baltimore's 76-acre county park with a two-mile loop through ravines and meadows along Walnut Creek and a faithful replica of an 1841 Pennsylvania German bank barn. Goldenrod Trail glows in fall.
when: Dawn to dusk, year-round

name: Lockville Canal Park
what: Walk among the stone remains of three Ohio & Erie Canal locks and through the 1888 Hartman No. 2 covered bridge, ten minutes from Canal Winchester. Free picnic shelter.
when: Dawn to dusk, year-round

name: Sycamore Creek Park
what: Pickerington's flagship park at the edge of Olde Village: multiple playgrounds, a ninja obstacle course, a stocked 2.3-acre pond, covered bridge, skate park, sledding hill and paths.
when: Daylight hours; restrooms seasonal

name: Groveport Heritage Park & Groveport Park
what: Heritage Park has the 1815 Groveport Log House, a stocked pond and a crushed-stone loop with a summer concert stage; nearby Groveport Park (7370 Groveport Rd) adds an EVOS playground, 1.8 miles of paved path, two fishing ponds and a canal lock.
when: Daylight hours, year-round; concerts seasonal

name: Hocking Hills State Park - Old Man's Cave
what: Ohio's most famous hike: a mile-long gorge of waterfalls, caves and stone bridges, with a visitor center, raptor enclosure and nearby Ash Cave (quarter-mile accessible trail), Cedar Falls and Rock House. No entry fee.
when: Dawn to dusk year-round; visitor center about 10am-4pm daily (seasonal)

name: Conkle's Hollow State Nature Preserve
what: A deep, cool gorge with a partly paved, mostly flat mile-long trail to a waterfall, which makes it the easiest Hocking Hills gorge for small kids. The rim loop is a steeper 2 miles. No pets.
when: Half hour before sunrise to half hour after sunset, year-round

name: Alum Creek State Park
what: Ohio's largest inland beach (3,000 feet of sand) on a 3,387-acre reservoir, plus a Storybook Trail, 20+ miles of mountain-bike trail, free disc golf and a dog park. No entrance fee for day use.
address: 3615 S Old State Rd, Delaware, OH 43015
when: Sunrise to sunset; beach open daylight hours in summer (no lifeguard)

name: Hoover Reservoir Park
what: City park on a 2,000-acre reservoir with a playground, paved path, disc golf, picnic shelter and greenway trailhead; a calm spot to watch boats and birds. Small-motor boats only, so it stays quiet.
when: 7am-11pm daily

name: Buckeye Lake State Park
what: Ohio's oldest state park: free beaches at Fairfield Beach, Brooks Park and Crystal Beach (Memorial Day to Labor Day), a 4.1-mile paved dam trail, playgrounds and fishing piers. Cranberry Bog is permit-only.
address: 2905 Liebs Island Rd NE, Millersport, OH 43046
when: 6am-11pm daily; beaches Memorial Day-Labor Day, daylight only

name: The Dawes Arboretum
what: Nearly 2,000 acres of trees, gardens, a Japanese garden and a drivable auto tour near Newark; admission is free every day. A good half-day trip east.
when: Grounds 7am to sunset, closed New Year's, Thanksgiving and Christmas; visitor center Mon-Sat 8am-5pm, Sun noon-5pm

name: Hanby House
what: Free tours of the Westerville home of Benjamin Hanby, who wrote 'Up on the Housetop' and 'Darling Nelly Gray', a stop on the Underground Railroad. Short visit; pair with Uptown Westerville.
when: Seasonal: Saturdays 1-4pm, June through September; other times by appointment
